claims.text: The as-synthesized HEA contains subtle local chemical clustering.
Local chemical clustering enhances local electron-phonon coupling.
Superconductivity in the selected HEA emerges through conventional isotropic s-wave BCS pairing.
Increasing local atomic ordering will strengthen the pairing interaction and raise Tc relative to a fully disordered baseline.
The initial HEA is homogeneous and fully chemically disordered.
The initial HEA crystallizes on a simple lattice such as bcc or CsCl-type.
Controlled annealing can induce local clustering and short-range ordering while preserving the overall composition and crystal structure.
Variations in local clustering and short-range chemical order modulate electron-phonon coupling strength.
Clustering-induced enhancement of electron-phonon coupling promotes isotropic s-wave pairing.
Enhanced electron-phonon coupling will increase the superconducting transition temperature.
The annealed sample will have a measurably higher Tc than the as-synthesized sample.
The annealed sample will show stronger superconducting-gap features in tunneling spectroscopy.
The annealed sample will show improved low-temperature transport consistent with enhanced electron-phonon coupling.
The unmodified HEA baseline has reproducible superconductivity with a standard weak-coupling BCS s-wave gap.
The proposed ordering effect should hold below 20 K for HEAs with similar compositional complexity and crystal structure.
The proposed mechanism may cease to apply when annealing causes phase segregation or a major structural transition.

contradictions.description: The as-synthesized state is said to contain subtle local chemical clustering in the hypothesis but is described as fully disordered and homogeneous in the initial-state field.
